# MORI TERRACE: visual references and rights

Asset: `public/models/external-v080/terraced-retail/terraced-retail.glb`.
Research and inspection date: 2026-10-07. This is an original game-ready interpretation of a building type inspired by the rebuilt Shibuya PARCO, not a surveyed or branded replica.

## Inspected photographs

The following four photographs were downloaded to temporary inspection storage and viewed as actual image pixels. They are not in this repository, are not GLB textures, and were not traced into copied graphics. No redistribution permission was established, so only source links are included.

Source page: [「渋谷PARCO」は屋外広場が魅力の建築, たてものフロンティア](https://tatefro.com/entry-93.html). The page displays 2021-06-23 / 2021-09-06 and a site copyright notice. Photographs depict the rebuilt building, not the pre-2019 PARCO.

- [Front / street elevation photograph](https://tatefro.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/shibuya-parco_outside_2-683x1024.jpg): large, nearly blank warm-white cladding blocks; narrow panel joints; deep horizontal terrace cuts; columns spanning the cuts; a tall glazed street frontage and recessed doors. An office tower rises behind the podium. Used to establish mass-to-glass ratio, not to copy shop logos.
- [Rear and office tower photograph](https://tatefro.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/shibuya-parco_outside_4-683x1024.jpg): blue-grey glazed upper tower with thin metal verticals and more opaque podium sides; planted wall area; pale sage ground-floor glazing. Used to differentiate the tower, side and rear facades.
- [Lower terrace photograph](https://tatefro.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/shibuya-parco_spiral-walk_3-1024x683.jpg): wood-like deck, shallow steps, slim frames, planted borders and small trees. Used to choose restrained material colours and terrace details.
- [Roof terrace photograph](https://tatefro.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/shibuya-parco_spiral-walk_5-1024x683.jpg): broad deck, long light-coloured bench-planters, glass edge rails, trees and stair connection beside the tower. Used to design original roof features.

## Primary-source architectural context

- [Takenaka Corporation, Shibuya PARCO / HULIC building](https://www.takenaka.co.jp/design/works/shibuya-parco-hulic-building/). Confirms commercial, theatre and office use; 19 above-ground floors plus 3 basement floors; 2017–2019 construction; building area 4,669.63 m². Describes the exterior circulation responding to Shibuya's streets and slopes. Its photographs were linked but local image downloads returned an anti-bot HTML document, so they were not claimed as pixel-inspected references.
- [PARCO architectural-design announcement, June 18, 2019](https://www.parco.co.jp/pdf/en/cname_20191009101341.pdf). Search-accessible source describes the outdoor paths and stairs rising to the tenth floor, and the faceted composition of the exterior. Used as architectural context, not a dimensional drawing.

## What is inferred or deliberately changed

Every asset measurement is a design estimate. Nominal footprint 60 × 50 m, podium roof 46.8 m and top 89.8 m are not measurements of PARCO. The model keeps the observed hierarchy of white podium blocks, terrace gaps, storefront glazing and upper tower while simplifying plan geometry. Its mass arrangement, stairs, bays, roof equipment, plants and `MORI TERRACE`, `FORM`, `KASA`, `NOVA` lettering are newly authored. No real PARCO, tenant or architect logo is included.

The source building's 19-floor count informs the broad ten-level commercial / nine-level tower concept. The asset has no surveyed floor plan, interior tenancy plan, basement or functioning navigable circulation. The photographs are a 2021 appearance reference and do not establish current tenant details.

## Distribution and license boundary

Reference images remain external links only. The deliverables contain procedural geometry, material colours and geometry lettering, with zero image textures or external URI dependencies. A third-party photo license does not attach copied photos to this submission because no photographs are bundled. No separate public license grant for the generated asset is asserted here; distribution remains under the repository owner's project terms.
